Subject: DPA: operational proofing for retention exceptions and residency carve-outs

Hi Alice —

Following our call yesterday, attaching the operational proposal for the retention carve-outs you asked about. High level: we can offer a narrow exception path for short-term incident evidence preservation (up to 45 days) for EU accounts, with strict audit and on-demand erasure flows.

Questions for you so we can finalize a redline:
- Do you need formal third-party certification of erasure (POE) or is our internal signed attestation sufficient?
- Do you expect the exception to apply to backups/snapshots as well, or only to live inference artifacts (tokens, KV cache)?
- Is a 45‑day maximum acceptable or should we consider a 60‑day operational window?

Attachments: redwood-retention-exceptions-ops-spec-v1.pdf (PDF), retention_matrix_atlaspay.xlsx (XLSX)

Thanks — I’ve looped in Grace from Legal and Priyom from Product to make sure the ops diagram and the legal language align.

—Camila

From: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@atlaspay.com>

Subject: Re: DPA: operational proofing for retention exceptions and residency carve-outs

Camila —

Thanks for the doc and the matrix. A few quick responses:
1) We need a formal proof-of-erasure (signed attestation) for the initial agreement; a third-party certificate is preferred but not mandatory at kickoff.
2) The exception should not apply to long-term backups or cold snapshots. It can apply to live system caches and ephemeral logs used for incident investigation.
3) 45 days is preferable; 60 days is borderline given our internal compliance.

Can you confirm how the erasure workflow will show evidence back to AtlasPay (S3 event + audit log + attestation PDF)? Also, what measures prevent cross-border replication during the exception window?

Best,
Alice
Alice Jensen
Senior Counsel, AtlasPay

Grace / Priyom —

Forwarding Alice's reply. They want: signed attestation (POE), no long-term backups included, and confirmation that cross-border replication is blocked during the exception. They prefer a 45‑day max.

Priyom: can you confirm the current runbook for incident evidence preservation (what we snapshot, where it lives, TTLs, how erasure is performed)? We need a short ops paragraph we can insert into the DPA: how evidence is retained, how we produce the attestation, and the audit log exports we’ll share.

Grace: legal wants wording that prevents the exception from being construed as a general residency carve-out. Suggested clause: "Limited operational preservation: For investigation of customer-specific security incidents, Provider may retain specified ephemeral inference artifacts for up to 45 days. This limited privilege shall not constitute data residency relocation and shall be subject to Provider attestation and export of audit evidence on request." Thoughts?

—Camila

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Thanks — quick tech note: our current incident flow snapshots in-region KV caches and ephemeral logs into a customer-scoped bucket in the same EU region. Backups and nightly snapshots are excluded by design. Deletion flow: we run an automated purge job that wipes the bucket objects and rotates keys; we then generate an audit export with object manifests and job run IDs.

We can provide:
- S3 event list + object manifest (CSV)
- Audit log slice (syslog timestamps + job IDs)
- A signed attestation PDF (signed by Redwood Security Lead) that references the manifests and job IDs

We enforce geofencing via access controls and do not replicate that bucket to other regions. I’ll add a short paragraph for the DPA describing the workflow.

—Priyom

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@atlaspay.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: operational proofing for retention exceptions and residency carve-outs

Alice / Camila / Priyom —

Appreciate the clear asks. Drafting guidance and proposed clause below (proposed redline language). Please review and flag any implementation mismatches.

Proposed clause (short):
"Operational Evidence Preservation: In the event of a documented customer-specific security incident, Provider may, for the sole purpose of investigation and remediation, preserve ephemeral inference artifacts and live caches for up to forty-five (45) calendar days. Such preservation shall be: (a) limited to artifacts generated in the same geographic region as the Customer; (b) excluded from Provider backups and archival snapshots; (c) subject to Provider-generated audit evidence (object manifests and audit logs) and a Provider-signed attestation of deletion upon completion of the preservation period or earlier upon Customer request. Preservation shall not be used for general processing outside the Customer’s region and shall not constitute a data residency transfer."

Operational notes for insertion in schedule: brief description of manifest+audit files, signature format, and timeframe for producing attestation (five business days after deletion).

If that wording is acceptable I’ll prepare a tracked version for the DPA.

—Grace
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: DPA: operational proofing for retention exceptions and residency carve-outs

Grace —

The proposed clause looks good. A couple of minor asks before we sign off:
- Please add language that the attestation will reference the HubSpot deal id and the object manifest IDs (helps our audit)
- Attestation turnaround: five business days is fine, but we need assurance that the manifest and audit slice is transmitted within one business day of deletion so we can ingest it into our compliance tooling.

If you can add those two items and send a tracked redline, we’ll review internally and aim to return a signed DPA by end of next week.

Thanks and that should close the retention/residency point for AtlasPay.

Best,
Alice
